content.title: What is an Interface?
content.description: An interface is a blueprint of a class that defines a contract of methods which implementing classes must provide. It supports abstraction and multiple inheritance in Java.

content.content: An interface specifies what a class should do rather than how it should do it. Classes implement interfaces using the implements keyword and provide implementations for the declared methods. Interfaces promote loose coupling and improve code flexibility.

content.title: Why Use Interfaces?
content.content: Interfaces enable abstraction, support multiple inheritance, improve code maintainability, and allow different classes to follow the same contract.
An interface is declared using the interface keyword. Its methods are public and abstract by default unless they are default or static methods.

content.title: Interface as a Contract
content.description: Every class implementing an interface must provide implementations for all of its abstract methods unless the class itself is declared abstract.

content.content: A class implements an interface using the implements keyword and defines the behavior of all declared methods.

content.title: Implementing an Interface

content.content: Java does not support multiple inheritance using classes, but it allows a class to implement multiple interfaces.

content.title: Multiple Interfaces

content.content: Since Java 8, interfaces can contain default and static methods, allowing common functionality without breaking existing implementations.

content.title: Default Method
Java 8 Feature
content.content: Default methods allow new functionality to be added to interfaces while maintaining backward compatibility.
An interface reference can refer to objects of any class that implements the interface. This supports runtime polymorphism.

items.question: Supports Multiple Inheritance
items.answer: A class can implement multiple interfaces simultaneously.

items.question: Promotes Loose Coupling
items.answer: Code depends on interfaces rather than concrete implementations.

items.question: Improves Flexibility
items.answer: Different classes can provide their own implementations of the same interface.

items.question: Encourages Reusability
items.answer: Common contracts can be reused across multiple projects.

content.title: Electrical Socket
content.content: An electrical socket defines a standard interface. Different devices like fans, chargers, and televisions can plug into the same socket while providing different functionality internally. Similarly, different classes implement the same interface in different ways.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: Interviewers frequently ask about interfaces, the difference between interfaces and abstract classes, multiple inheritance, default methods, static methods, and interface-based polymorphism.

items.question: Can an interface be instantiated?
items.answer: No. Objects cannot be created directly from an interface.

items.question: Can a class implement multiple interfaces?
items.answer: Yes. Java fully supports multiple interface implementation.

items.question: Must implemented methods be public?
items.answer: Yes. Interface methods are public by default, so implementing methods must also be public.

content.title: Remember This
content.description: Interfaces define contracts, not implementations. They enable abstraction, multiple inheritance, and runtime polymorphism while keeping applications loosely coupled.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Classes use the implements keyword to implement interfaces.
A class can implement multiple interfaces.
Default and static methods were introduced in Java 8.
Interfaces support abstraction and runtime polymorphism.
